import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR"""

df = pd.read_csv(pd.compat.StringIO(data))

sns.set(style="whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
scatter = sns.scatterplot(x='model_year', y='price_usd', hue='sensor_type', size='megapixels', sizes=(50, 200), data=df, legend='full')

# Adding labels
for index, row in df.iterrows():
    plt.text(row['model_year'], row['price_usd'], f"{row['brand']} {row['model_year']}",
             verticalalignment='bottom', horizontalalignment='left', color='black')

plt.title('Camera Price vs Model Year by Sensor Type and Megapixels')
plt.xlabel('Model Year')
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)')
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

This visualization shows how price varies with model year, differentiated by sensor type, and the size of the markers indicates the megapixel count. The labels make it easy to identify each data point. That should be insightful.
